_comment: Route challenges for the UGA demo. Each item is anchored to one or more lanelet relation IDs from the .osm; the viewer highlights those lanelet surfaces in the category colour and shows the note on hover. Add more IDs to a 'lanelets' array to extend a difficulty over more of the road.

categories.label: Unmarked
categories.desc: Unmarked two-way rural road — no pavement markings, so lane position must be inferred from the road edges.

categories.label: Rural two-way road
categories.desc: Rural two-way road — undivided, oncoming traffic shares a narrow corridor.

categories.label: Wide multi-lane road
categories.desc: Wide multi-lane cross-section — three-lane centre-turn or divided five-lane arterial.

categories.label: Change direction
categories.desc: The route changes direction here — a connected turn linking two road segments, where the vehicle must track the heading change and give way as needed.

items.desc: No pavement markings, so the vehicle must hold its lane from the road edges alone. Level grade with two curves and a curb-and-gutter edge (~0.1 mi).
No markings, with multiple grade changes and multiple curves over ~1.08 mi. Partial tree canopy and potential flooding add perception and traction risk.
No markings, multiple bumps and a curve, with an enclosed tree canopy, no shoulder and falling branches — the most hazardous stretch (~0.41 mi).
Clear centre and edge lines, but multiple grade changes over ~0.69 mi and only a narrow paved shoulder leave little room for error.
Clear centreline but no edge lines, with multiple bumps and a curve under partial canopy and a narrow paved shoulder (~0.22 mi).
Clear centreline but no edge lines on a downhill grade and a gentle left curve; the shared centre lane adds turning and merging complexity (~0.43 mi).
Clear centre and edge lines on an uphill grade and a gentle left curve, with higher speeds and more lane changes across the wide cross-section (~0.25 mi).
A connected turn where the route changes direction, linking two road segments across five lanelets — the vehicle must track the heading change and yield as needed.
